q: 1. A drawn back of bar chart is
options: it is difficult to judge whether an activity is completed or not
all the activities represented are independent of each other
sequence of activities is not clearly defined
it is not possible to judge whether the activity is ahead or behind the schedule
explain: While progress can be marked, the primary structural drawback is that the specific logical sequence and dependencies between activities are not explicitly defined.

q: 2. Milestone charts are developed in
explain: Milestone charts were developed as an improvement over the basic bar chart around 1940 AD.

q: 3. The earliest method used for planning of projects was
explain: The bar chart (Gantt chart), developed in the early 1900s, predates CPM and PERT (developed in the 1950s) as a project planning tool.

q: 4. The optimistic time represents the
options: shortest possible time in which an activity can be completed if everything goes exceptionally well
time in which the activity is normally expected to complete under normal contingencies
time in which an activity will take to complete in case of difficulty
explain: Optimistic time (to) is the minimum time an activity could take assuming ideal conditions with no complications.

q: 5. Choose the incorrect statement
options: arrow representing activity in CPM network is drawn without any scale
head of an activity represents the finish of an activity
tail of an activity represents the start of an activity
explain: All the statements provided (a, b, and c) are actually correct definitions within CPM networking; therefore, none are incorrect.

q: 6. Gantt Bar chart is drawn for
explain: A Gantt chart explicitly plots individual activities (vertical axis) against time or duration (horizontal axis).

q: 7. The maximum number of tail event occurring in a CPM is
explain: A standard project network should have only one single start event (tail event) from which the project begins.

q: 8. Latest finish time in CPM technique is indicated by
explain: Standard CPM notation uses rectangles (or squares) to denote time values like Latest Finish Time.

q: 9. Use of dummies is required for
explain: Dummies give unique event numbering (the 'grammatical' purpose) and show correct dependencies (the 'logical' purpose).

q: 10. Critical path is
options: shortest path for the earliest completion of the project
longest path of the network from the first event to the last event
ideal path by preceeding along which the project can be completed as per the schedule
the path which takes into account the completion of all the parallel activities
explain: The critical path is the specific sequence of activities that must be completed exactly as scheduled to finish the project on time.

q: 11. Which of the following in a CPM network activity?
explain: In CPM, an 'activity' is an active process that consumes time and resources; 'excavation' is a clear action, while the others are often viewed as states/events.

q: 12. Which of the following terminology is not relevant to a CPM planning?
explain: Optimistic time is a PERT term (part of the three-estimate approach), not used in CPM which relies on single deterministic durations.

q: 13. An event is
options: a definite position of an activity
explain: Per the answer key, d. An event is an instant at which activities start or finish.

q: 14. When all the paths are arranged according to the descending order of the float, the path which is next to critical path is known as
explain: The path with the next-lowest float after the critical path (zero float) is termed the secondary critical path.

q: 15. CPM stands for
explain: CPM = Critical Path Method.

q: 16. PERT analysis is based on
explain: PERT analysis uses all three time estimates - optimistic, pessimistic, and most likely - to compute the expected activity duration.

q: 17. In a time-cost optimization using CPM the crashing of the activities along the critical path is done starting with the activity having
options: crashing has no relation with cost slope
explain: To reduce project duration most economically, we crash the critical activity that has the lowest cost slope (cheapest to crash first).

q: 18. Earliest finish of an activity is always
options: greater than earliest event time of the following node
less than earliest event time of the following node
less than or equal to earliest event time of the following node
greater than or equal to earliest event time of the following node
explain: The following node's earliest time is the maximum of the earliest finishes of all activities entering it, so EF ≤ it.

q: 19. If t0, tp and tm are the optimistic, pessimistic and most likely time estimates of an activity respectively, the expected time t of the activity will be
explain: The PERT expected time formula is te = (t0 + 4tm + tp)/6, giving greatest weight to the most likely time.

q: 20. In PERT, optimistic time in which any activity can possibly be accomplished
options: the minimum time in which any activity can possibly be accomplished
the maximum time which an activity might require
the time which has the highest probability of occurrence
explain: Optimistic time ($t_o$) assumes everything goes perfectly, representing the minimum possible duration.

q: 21. If TL is the latest allowable event occurrence time, total activity slacks (S), is equal to
explain: Total float/slack can be equivalently computed as LST-EST, LFT-EFT, or TL-EFT, all giving the same result - so all of the above is correct.

q: 22. The slack for an event i is given by
explain: Slack for an event is calculated as the Latest Allowable occurrence time ($T_L$) minus the Earliest Expected occurrence time ($T_E$).

q: 23. A dummy activity is that part of the project which
explain: A dummy activity has zero duration and consumes no resources; it exists only to maintain correct network logic.

q: 24. t^{ij} and t_E^{ij} indicates the time required for completion of an activity in CPM and PERT respectively. Here the subscript E stands for
explain: In PERT, subscript E denotes the expected time accounting for uncertainty[cite: 1].

q: 25. Total project time is the
options: sum of duration of all activities
sum of duration of non-critical activities
sum of duration of critical activities
explain: The total project duration is determined by the length of the critical path, which is the sequence of activities with the longest total duration.

q: 26. The technique for establishing and maintaining priorities among the various jobs of a project, is known as
explain: Critical Ratio is a priority index determined by dividing the time remaining until a job is due by the work time remaining.

q: 27. Any delay in starting, that involves consumption of any of the interfering floats of an activity, will result in
explain: Using interfering float reduces the float of later activities but does not by itself delay the project.

q: 28. Negative slack occurs
options: when latest allowable time is greater than earliest expected time
when events stick to their schedule
explain: Negative slack typically arises due to deficiency of resources causing the schedule to fall behind requirements.

q: 29. The amount of time by which the activity completion can be delayed without interfering with the start of succeeding activity, is known as
explain: That is the definition of free float.

q: 30. The time by which a particular activity can be delayed without affecting the proceeding and succeeding activities is known as
explain: Independent float specifically measures the delay possible in an activity without affecting either the preceding or succeeding activities.

q: 31. Slack time in PERT analysis
options: can never be greater than zero
is always zero for critical activities
can never be less than zero
explain: Critical activities/events in PERT always have zero slack, as they lie directly on the critical path with no room for delay.

q: 32. The first stage of a large construction work to
explain: A project begins with conception of the idea.

q: 33. When the time of earliest finish and the latest finish are equal in an operation, the operation is called
explain: Zero float (EF = LF) means the activity is critical.

q: 34. A drawback of the bar chart is that
options: all the activity are independent of each other
it is difficult to judge whether an activity is completed or not
the sequence of activity is not clearly defined
explain: Per the answer key, c: bar charts do not clearly show the sequence.

q: 35. Select the incorrect statement
options: a critical path always begins at the very first event
a critical path always terminates at the last event
critical activities control the project duration
critical activity is the one for which free float is zero
explain: Per the answer key, d. Critical activities have zero total float, so the statement about free float is the incorrect one.

q: 36. In the given figure, the network of a project represents
options: activity of an excavation of a footing
activity of an excavation which starts at event No. 1 and ends at even No. 2
activity of excavation which takes 8 units of time
explain: The figure shows the excavation activity between events 1 and 2 labeled with duration '8', indicating it takes 8 units of time to complete.

q: 37. If for a activity optimistic time is 1 day pessimistic times is 8 days and most likely time is 3 days then the expected time is
explain: The most likely time is cut off in the scan. The key answer 3.5 follows from tE = (1 + 4m + 8)/6 with m = 3 days.

q: 38. A Milestone chart
options: shows the interdependencies of various jobs
depicts the delay of jobs, if any
points outgoing ahead of schedule of jobs, if any
explain: A milestone chart does not show interdependencies between jobs (that's a network diagram's function), so per the answer key, none of these accurately describes it fully.

q: 39. Positive float for any activity means that the activity is
explain: Positive float means sub-critical.

q: 40. Project control begins early in the project with planning and ends late in the project with
explain: Project control spans from early planning through to a final post-implementation review at project closeout.

q: 41. Float is
options: the earliest time by which an activity may commence
lastest time by which an activity can be delayed without hapering the completion of the project
lastest allowable time - earliest expected time
time available time required for an activity
explain: Per the answer key, d: float is the time available minus the time required.

q: 42. Which of the following is a weakness of bar chart?
explain: Per the answer key, all of the above.
